t: Daily wird of ḥasbunā Allāh
p: That God be one's reckoner and trustee in all affairs, suffice against all creation, give victory, put one's love in hearts, and enrich from His bounty; a guarded fortress (ḥirz manīʿ).
tm: Every day and night; any time.

t: Swift removal of hardships — the four Names
p: Quick removal of pressing matters; victory over enemies; love of the world; honour among creation.

t: Recitation pattern with al-Anfāl 8:62–64
p: Attain what one hopes for; God is his sufficiency in this world and the next.

t: Reaching rulers, ministers and people of rank — the 8:62 table
p: To reach and be received by emirs, ministers and lords.

t: Lasting honour, sufficiency, strength and gentleness in hardships
p: Permanent ʿizz, kifāya, quwwa and luṭf in difficulties.

t: Money from the unseen — the Kāfī / Ghanī / Mughnī / Fattāḥ duʿāʾ
p: Dirhams 'from the unseen of God'; a khādim of the Names brings extra spending money, possibly found each morning by one's head.
tm: Every night, until it opens. 'Whoever keeps to the door of the Real is never turned away.'

t: Each Name by its own number, after every prayer
p: Affairs settled and made easy so one needs no one; especially matters of worldly livelihood.

t: Drawing hearts and gathering the public — Daʿwat al-Taskhīr
p: Jalb al-qulūb, people gathering to you.

t: Seven-day riyāḍa — the khādim as a sultan; the sword and the ring
p: The verse's khādim appears on the 7th day 'in the likeness of a worldly sultan'; he gives a sword of light and a white ring for entering on kings.

t: Extinguishing enemies' fire — 3-day fast from Tuesday
p: Against enemies (sickening, scattering them). The book's harshest section.

t: Cutting off tyrants — night prayer sets with 950
p: Against tyrants and people of corruption.

t: Saturday before sunrise — 1000 + 5:59–60
p: Against an unjust oppressor.

t: The seven ṭarīqas by prayer time — counts as 'swords'
p: A graded programme against an oppressor across the day.

t: Ṭarīqa 8 — affection and joining (taʿṭīf, taʾlīf)
p: Affection and harmony 'so the sought one does not leave the seeker's obedience for a single breath'.

t: Riyāḍa for unveiling — write, drink, sleep
p: Mukāshafāt; a dream guide shows what you intended (e.g. buried treasure, 'dafīn').
tm: Choose a month whose first day is a Thursday. On Thursday night (laylat al-jumuʿa) break fast on nuql (dried fruit and nuts), sugar and barley bread. 5 or 7 nights with fasting; the 7th night in an empty house.

t: Sayings on counts: 450, 1000, 4000
p: Short counts quoted from 'some of the gnostics'.

t: The Daʿwa — 'Sayf al-Awliyāʾ'
p: The supplication referred to throughout Bāb 2.

t: The jadwal for entering on rulers — full-moon night
p: Entering on kings, ministers and rulers in God's guarded fortress; no one reaches you with harm; release from an oppressor.
tm: Write on the night of the 13th or 14th of the lunar month.

t: Same jadwal under the pillow — provision in 19 days
p: Finding spending money within 19 days.

t: At-Tawba 9:129 — Saturday and for affection
p: Two uses of 9:129.

t: The 4×4 ḥasbunā word-square (carried for vengeance)
p: A jadwal the practitioner carries 'if he seeks vengeance from enemies'.

t: Love — the jadwal hung in a pomegranate-wood frame
p: Moving and drawing a person's spirituality in affection; 'the ring turns' as a sign the spirits have come.

t: Seven-day khalwa for provision — the circle and 44 paper coins
p: Abundant livelihood and spending from the unseen. The author warns it must be done for God, 'otherwise ruin is feared for him'.

t: The Ikhlāṣ purse — never-ending spending money
p: Finding one's spending money in the purse; spending without counting, 'it never runs out'.

t: The Ikhlāṣ purse — variant with ten silver coins
p: Same purse, charged with silver.

t: 19,000 — summoning a person through the khuddām
p: The sought person comes in the morning 'humble and obedient, even if a king'.

t: 1,313 after every prayer — freedom and wealth
p: The captive is freed, the imprisoned released, the fearful made safe, the poor enriched, the humbled honoured; subduing tyrants.

t: Ṣalāt al-Fatḥ wa-l-Qurb (Ibn Mashīsh)
p: Opening of arrival and nearness to the Prophet ﷺ. Keep it at the beginning and end of every working.

t: Love, awe and reverence — the Ḥafīẓ / Qahhār duʿāʾ
p: People turn to you with love, awe and respect; protection; victory.

t: Wealth within a week — 313 after Ṣubḥ and ʿAṣr
p: For someone short of money: wide provision; 'the world comes to him entire'.

t: The seals (khawātim) and Name-awfāq of the duʿāʾ
p: Six small seals for the Names, the large seal of the verse, and four more; love and acceptance.

t: Seven days from Sunday — the khādim as a youth in green; the Sulaymān ring
p: Learning the secret of the daʿwa; a ring for commanding jinn.

t: Uses of the ring and daʿwa: news, relief, fever
p: Asking about the absent or the sick; relief; fevers.

t: Brick into fire, and the gnostic who forgave
p: An operation against a person, with a story.

t: Obedience of enviers; leadership; open doors
p: Enviers, stubborn people and oppressors obey; freedom from the whisperer and the commanding self.

t: Seven-night khalwa — lights, six angels, twelve, then a king
p: Opening of the daʿwa's secret.

t: Victory over an adversary — the verse on white cloth in the hour of Mercury
p: Victory over an adversary in a dispute; protection from beasts and weapons (the seal).
tm: Saturday, in the hour of Mercury, with the Moon well-aspected (masʿūd).

t: Removing enmity — the 7×7 square of 'wa-ttabaʿū riḍwāna-llāh'
p: Ends opposition and quarrelling between two disputants.

t: Protection duʿāʾs: oppressor, veiling, sunrise ḥirz
p: Freedom from injustice; veiling from enemies; protection from every devil, ruler, beast and danger.

t: Provision — the 5×5 square with an empty centre (Razzāq · Wahhāb · Fattāḥ · Ghanī · Muʿṭī)
p: Seeking provision. 'It needs no ascendant, no observation, no hour.'
tm: 8 days; 'the answer is nearer than that'.

t: Unveiling of knowledge — Hādī · Khabīr · Mubīn · ʿAllām al-Ghuyūb
p: 'A true unveiling of all you want'; influence in the world.

t: Hādī — silver ring; infant nursing; guidance in darkness
p: Success in all good deeds; an infant who will not nurse starts nursing; guided on the road in darkness.

t: Khabīr — iron ring on Friday; dream news
p: Told in sleep what will happen in the world tomorrow.

t: Matīn — four works: banner, indigo garment, the afflicted, iron knife
p: Driving off enemies; restraining the self from lusts; burning jinn (exorcism); dealing with kings.

t: Dhū l-Jalāl wa-l-Ikrām — Saturn ring of red copper; olive-wood cup; lead in the net
p: Whatever is asked is given; abundance in a region; protection from enemies; a fisherman's catch increases.

t: Duʿāʾ 'Yā man lā tarāhu l-ʿuyūn'
p: Kept continuously: success and answered supplication.

t: Taskhīr — Ḥannān Mannān in a 5×5 with empty centre
p: Subjection and drawing of hearts.

t: Awe and rank — Mutaʿāl · ʿAzīz · ʿAẓīm · Rafīʿ · ʿAlī · Kabīr
p: Everyone who looks at you holds you in awe.

t: Al-Malik al-Mumīt square; other operations against oppressors
p: Several further operations against oppressors.

t: Counts and durations (rulers, wealth, unveiling)
p: A list of programmes with numbers.

t: Silver ring of the verse; ring of the seven metals; mastic
p: Sultans subjected; lasting greatness; lasting fortune.
tm: Hour of Jupiter, Thursday; Saturn in exaltation (Libra).

t: Traveller's protection — the seven pebbles and the four archangels
p: Protection of the traveller: 'you will see nothing you dislike'.

t: Home and goods: corners of the house; protection from weevils
p: House and family protected; a good life and righteous children; goods kept from insects.

t: The great seal of the verse — 3×3 of 450 on white silk
p: Great effect in all one's works; also used against an oppressor.

t: Second 3×3 seal (198–206, constant 606)
p: Printed after the 450 seal without its own label.

t: How to work any of these (taṣrīf) — the general method
p: The book's general frame for every working.

t: Al-Yāfiʿī's circle (dāʾira)
p: Everything sought becomes easy; a beast becomes tame; cold fevers removed; a king carrying it is loved and held in awe; relief, an open chest, good character.

t: Table of al-Anfāl 8:62 — the printed number 1336 is its abjad
p: Reaching rulers and people of rank (same as 14-03/14-04).

t: Money from the unseen — 450 or 4,500 each night?
p: Same as 14-06/14-07 (Kāfī · Ghanī · Mughnī · Fattāḥ).

t: Bāb 2 in the English — its sword numbers are wrong
p: Records only where the translation differs from the Arabic. The operations themselves stay summarised under 14-10 to 14-13.

t: Unveiling riyāḍa — midnight confirmed; 7th night 700 or 7,000
p: Same as 14-15.
tm: Thursday night that falls on the first of the month. Break fast on fried fruit or nuts, sugar and barley bread. At  midnight  the verse 950×.

t: At-Tawba 9:129 on Saturday — 1000× for a need, 41× for affection
p: The English gives the benign reading of the Saturday use.

t: Love square on the pomegranate tripod — the verse 950×, opened with the basmala
p: Same as 14-22. Corrects one reading.

t: Seven-day provision khalwa — English counts and the layout of the circle
p: Same as 14-23.

t: Ikhlāṣ purse — English counts are lower
p: Same as 14-24.

t: After every prayer: 313 or 1,313?
p: Same as 14-27.

t: Ḥafīẓ / Qahhār duʿāʾ — the garbled letters read "Fajash Thatkhaz"
p: Same as 14-29.

t: Wealth within a week — 303 or 313?
p: Same as 14-30.

t: The seals of the duʿāʾ — what the English copy shows
p: Same as 14-31 and 14-32.

t: Fever seal — built on the ḥawqala
p: For curing fever; reciting the verse over it is better.

t: Names-squares — oppressor and unveiling counts differ
p: Same as 14-31.

t: Seven-night khalwa — night 2 is the invocation 100×
p: Same as 14-36. Settles an open question.

t: Dispute seal — made from the words of 3:173–174
p: Same as 14-37: Saturday, hour of Mercury, Moon benefic; on a white rag, placed on the head.

t: Provision 5×5 — total 2000 confirmed; 1900 is the recitation count
p: Same as 14-40. Settles most of question 2.

t: Dhū l-Jalāl wa-l-Ikrām — 313 confirmed; the stone; the jug; the rats
p: Same as 14-45, with corrections and one more use.

t: Rising in degrees — four Names 1000× after every prayer
p: Hidden treasures of the earth and people's thoughts shown; after three weeks, the unseen of the heavens and earth.
tm: 7 days, then three weeks of training.

t: Veiling from sight — the verse 7,050 and Yā-Sīn 36:1–9
p: Not seen by those who want to harm you: 'if all the people of the heavens and earth conspired to harm you, they could not.'

t: Freeing a prisoner, relieving sadness — 7,056 after the night prayer
p: The prisoner is saved; grief lifts.

t: In a critical situation — 4 rakʿas and 'Yā man lā tarāhu l-ʿuyūn'
p: The hardship goes away.

t: Ḥannān Mannān 5×5 — 250 confirmed
p: Same as 14-47.

t: Awe square — constant 2367 = the six Names with al-Mutaʿālī
p: Same as 14-48.

t: Squares against oppressors (al-Muhlik al-Mumīt, 585)
p: Recorded as headings only, as with 14-49.

t: Protection from what one fears — az-Zukhruf 43:13 with al-Laṭīf al-Khabīr
p: God protects him from what he fears.

t: Mālik al-Mulk · Qayyūm · Bāqī table
p: A table for these three Names.

t: Count variants and short uses (English)
p: Short programmes from the end of the book.

t: Tried and tested for fear — "I have placed myself in the protection of Allah"
p: Protection from fear.

p: Chart I of the compilation (p.16): the abjad — the twenty-eight letters in four columns by element (fire, earth, air, water), each with its name and value, in abjad order cycling through the elements. Every value agrees with the engine's table.

t: Writing pattern interleaving Surat al-Fātiḥa with the Qur'anic disconnected letters [ḥurūf
p: Writing pattern interleaving Surat al-Fātiḥa with the Qur'anic disconnected letters [ḥurūf-i muqaṭṭaʿ'a] — five columns read right to left, alternating a row of Fātiḥa words with a row of isolated letter- groups. no labels.

t: 3×3 wafq
p: 3×3 wafq (the classic buduh square) — angel names written around the border in Arabic, Gabriel [Jibrīl] above and Michael [Mīkāʾīl] at the left, with further names and invocations along the right, foot and corner diagonals.

t: Talismanic strip
p: Talismanic strip — a row of Arabic numerals ruled underneath, closing at the left with a single sigil character; no labelling.

t: Circular talisman
p: Circular talisman — 5×5 numerical wafq at the centre, its middle cell marked "the request" [ḥāja]; around it concentric rings divided into eight compartments naming the presiding angels and jinn kings in Arabic, the outer segments filled with talismanic script.

t: A manuscript eightfold of Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ
p: A manuscript eightfold of Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ (p.2273), the sura's words run down the square one word further each row as on p.2271, inside a frame inscribed with the names of the Prophet and the four caliphs (Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, ʿUmar al-Fārūq …) and of the prophets (Ibrāhīm Khalīl Allāh …). Cited from the facsimile.

t: If you wish to beat and whip the jinn afflicting the patient
p: A ruled frame (p.2295) holding Yaʿūj, Bayʿūj, Dayʿūj with Q 10:59 and Q 57:13 (fa-ḍuriba baynahum bi-sūrin lahu bābun …), numbers and letters at the sides and corners. Cited from the figure.

t: To expel the jinn afflicting a patient from the patient's body
p: Row of talismanic characters — three hooked strokes, six pentagrams flanking a central interlaced knot-seal, and three upright strokes; no text.

t: For a binding not yet a year old
p: Row of talismanic characters — a pair of barred crossed strokes, a pentagram, a hooked glyph, a small circle, a three-legged figure and four upright strokes; no text.

t: A line of the seven seal-signs and further signs
p: A line of the seven seal-signs and further signs (p.2329): the star, the strokes, the lattice, mīm, hā and wāw with a row of ʿayn-like marks. Cited from the figure.

t: Single row of talismanic cipher characters
p: Single row of talismanic cipher characters — a run of repeated ha' letters, a dotted cross-sign, a series of 'ayn marks and a flourish; no text.

t: The index of the divine names with their values
p: The index of the divine names with their values (p.2390), names 1–48 in the order of the hadith list. Its values agree with the engine's, and it gives the right values where the table of p.1439 slips: Mutaʿālī 541, Rāfiʿ 351, Wālī 47.

t: Table of the Beautiful Names of God with their numerical values, entries 1–48
p: Table of the Beautiful Names of God with their numerical values, entries 1–48 — two side-by-side column groups, each headed: place in the sequence [sirasi]; the name [isim]; its numerical value [ʿadad].

t: The index of the divine names, continued
p: The index of the divine names, continued (p.2392), names 51–96.

t: Continuation of the table of the divine names and their numerical values, entries 51–96
p: Continuation of the table of the divine names and their numerical values, entries 51–96 (column headings cut off above) — same paired groups: place in the sequence [sirasi]; the name [isim]; its numerical value [ʿadad].

t: The back cover of the compilation
p: The back cover of the compilation (p.2401): the emblem, the title Iḥyāʾ Uṣūl al-Ḥikmah, the attribution to Aḥmad ibn ʿAlī al-Būnī, a note that the book is a work of khidma offered freely and not for sale, and the date August 2026.

t: Renewal before worship
p: Taʿawwudh and Basmala · Shahāda ×3 · Istighfār ×100 · Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ ×3

ref: Daily · Daily — opens every wird and every holy night
t: Adab al-Ṭarīqa (Naqshbandī)
p: Niyya · Shahāda ×3 · Astaghfiru-llāh ×70 · Rābiṭa sharīfa · al-Fātiḥa ×1 — intending the manifestations and protection descending in Makka · Āmana r-Rasūl (Q 2:285–286) · Sūrat al-Sharḥ ×7 · Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ ×11 · al-Falaq ×1, al-Nās ×1 · Lā ilāha illā-llāh ×10, after the last: Muḥammadun Rasūlu-llāh · Ṣalawāt ×10 (Allāhumma ṣalli ʿalā Muḥammadin wa ʿalā āli Muḥammadin wa sallim) · al-Ṣalawāt al-Sh

t: al-Awrād al-Qudsiyya — Ḥizb of Shāh Naqshband
p: Elders of the order agree it serves all needs, wards off calamity, eases hardship, increases nearness, brings insight and healing.

ref: Daily · Daily, one ḥizb per weekday (Mon→Sun, 8th on Monday)
t: Dalāʾil al-Khayrāt — ḥizb of the day
p: Mawlana Shaykh Nazim: recite the Dalāʾil for all your problems. In Ramaḍān, 1 juzʾ of Dalāʾil between ʿAṣr and Maghrib.

ref: Daily · Daily, one portion per weekday
t: al-Ṣalāt al-Kubrā — portion of the day
p: Traditionally recited whole; the seven-day division is for those beginning. Primary purpose: love and sulūk. Seek ijāza from your own shaykh.

ref: Daily · Once after Fajr (seeker); morning + after Maghrib is the most complete
t: Ḥizb al-Wiqāya — Ibn ʿArabī
p: After Fajr ×1 — for the seeker on the path · After ʿAṣr ×1, preceded by Sūrat al-Wāqiʿa — provision, relief of poverty · Morning ×1 and after Maghrib ×1 — the most complete method · ×3 after two rakʿas of Ṣalāt al-Ḥāja — for needs · ×41 in one sitting for weighty matters (may be shared among a group); fast that day and give discreet ṣadaqa

t: Duʿāʾ al-Ḥifẓ (protection)
p: Recommended 7× daily by Mawlana Shaykh Nazim.

t: Ḥizb al-Baḥr — with Iʿtiṣām and Ikhtitām
p: Protection from the evil ones and their attacks; pairs with the Ṣalāt al-Mashīshiyya (Ibn Mashīsh's ṣalawāt and his successor's ḥizb go together).

ref: Daily · Daily (often before sleep — good dreams)
t: al-Ṣalāt al-Mashīshiyya
p: Recite the ṣalāt · Allāh Allāh Allāh — each “āh” extended about 12 counts · Q 28:85 and Q 18:10 (end of older copies); some add Q 33:56

t: Ḥizb al-Barr (al-Ḥizb al-Kabīr)
p: The Great Ḥizb is recited after Fajr; opens with Āyat al-Istiftāḥ (Q 6:54) — hope for the repentant.

t: One juzʾ of Qurʾān
p: Sohbah of Mawlana Shaykh Mehmet: “A Juz of the Qurʾān must be read daily.” Yā Sīn at the beginning of the day — wants supplied (Mishkāt 2177).

t: Counting the 99 Names
p: Whoever counts them every day enters Paradise; make duʿāʾ with them. The Greatest Name is sought through worship, given to the one who deserves it, and is for īmān, not dunyā.

t: Friday Ṣalawāt — Kunūz al-Asrār
p: Mawlana Shaykh Nazim's Friday ṣalawāt (Kunūz al-Asrār).

t: Special litany for spiritual and physical wealth
p: Renew the shahāda · Lā ilāha illā-llāh ×100, then Muḥammadun Rasūlu-llāh once · Mā shāʾa-llāh ×100 · al-ḥamdu li-llāh ×100 · Shukran li-llāh ×100 · Subḥāna-llāh ×100 · Astaghfiru-llāh ×100 · Innā li-llāhi wa innā ilayhi rājiʿūn ×100 · Ḥasbunā-llāhu wa niʿma l-wakīl ×100 · Tawakkaltu ʿala-llāh ×100 · Lā ḥawla wa lā quwwata illā bi-llāhi l-ʿaliyyi l-ʿaẓīm ×100 · Naqshbandī Ihdāʾ, al-Fātiḥa

t: Rajab — daily duties of the month
p: Astaghfiru-llāh 100–1000 · Lā ilāha illā-llāh 100–1000 · Ṣalawāt 100–1000 · Yā Laṭīf 100–500 · Rajab 1–10: Subḥāna-llāhi l-Ḥayyi l-Qayyūm ×100 · Rajab 11–20: Subḥāna-llāhi l-Aḥadi ṣ-Ṣamad ×100 · Rajab 21–30: Subḥāna-llāhi r-Raʾūf ×100 · Sūrat al-Anʿām every day · One juzʾ of Qurʾān daily · Dalāʾil al-Khayrāt — the day's ḥizb · Prayer of Rajab: 30 rakʿas across the month in twos — each rakʿa Fātiḥa

ref: Occasion · month 7 day first Thursday night
t: Laylat al-Raghāʾib
p: After ʿIshāʾ: Adab al-Ṭarīqa · The Grand Transmitted Duʿāʾ of Grandshaykh ʿAbdallāh (ad-Duʿāʾ al-Maʾthūr) · Ṣalāt al-Tasābīḥ 4 rakʿas · Ṣalāt al-Shukr 2 rakʿas · Sunnat al-Raghāʾib prayer (details on @MawlanaSultan)

t: Isrāʾ wa-l-Miʿrāj
p: Night: Niyya; Adab al-Ṭarīqa; the Grand Transmitted Duʿāʾ of Grandshaykh; Khatm al-Khwājagān and dhikr; read the Mawlid · Ṣalāt al-Tasābīḥ 4; Ṣalāt al-Shukr 2 with Qunūt · Ṣalāt al-Miʿrāj 2 rakʿas: each Fātiḥa + Ikhlāṣ ×20 (Shaykh Adnan's sheet: Shukr 2 with Ikhlāṣ ×3; Sunnat al-Miʿrāj 2 with Ikhlāṣ ×21) · Ihdāʾ, duʿāʾ and Fātiḥa · Shaykh Nāẓim: complete 1000 Ikhlāṣ, 1000 lā ilāha illā-llāh, 1000

t: Shaʿbān — month of ṣalawāt
p: Astaghfiru-llāh 70–700 · Ikhlāṣ 100–1000 · Lā ilāha illā-llāh 100–1000 · Allāh 5000–10,000 (with the tongue and on the heart) · Āyat al-Kursī ×40 · Ṣalawāt 100 – 1000 – 10,000 · Recite the Ṣalāt al-Kubrā — Shaʿbān is the month of ṣalawāt

t: Ramaḍān — Adab and Awrād
p: Last third of the night after Ṣalāt al-Wuḍūʾ: Niyya (Nawaytu l-arbaʿīn…), Adab al-Ṭarīqa, Marḥaban duʿāʾ (from 15th: al-Widāʿ), Duʿāʾ al-Maʾthūr · Complete the awrād in three windows: last third → sunrise; ʿAṣr → Maghrib; Maghrib → ʿIshāʾ · Between ʿAṣr and Maghrib: 1–3 juzʾ of Qurʾān and 1 juzʾ of Dalāʾil · Before Tarāwīḥ: taʿawwudh, basmala, shahāda ×3, istighfār ×100, Ikhlāṣ ×3, then the fastin

t: Eve of 16 Ramaḍān — night of Ṣāḥib al-Zamān
p: Witr split 2+1; after the two: ṣalawāt and Yā Aḥad · Sūrat al-Aʿlā / al-Kāfirūn / three Quls on the 16th night and Laylat al-Qadr

t: Laylat al-Qadr — adab of Grandshaykh and Mawlana
p: Ghusl one hour before Maghrib on their intention · Niyya: nawaytu-l-arbaʿīn, nawaytu-l-ʿuzla, nawaytu-l-khalwa, nawaytu-l-iʿtikāf, nawaytu-s-sulūk, nawaytu-r-riyāḍa… · 2 rakʿas sunnat al-ghusl; Adab al-Ṭarīqa; Duʿāʾ al-Maʾthūr · Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ with all awrād; renew fasting niyya; 20 Tarāwīḥ · Ṣalāt al-Tasbīḥ 4, Ṣalāt al-Shukr 2, Witr with Qunūt · Short Khatm al-Khwājagān · 100 rakʿas in twos:

t: Last night of Ramaḍān and ʿĪd
p: After Witr, stand toward the qibla: 100 ṣalawāt, gifting the month's worship as Mawlid to the Prophet ﷺ · Pay Zakāt al-Fiṭr before the ʿĪd prayer · Keep the ʿĪd night alive; takbīr, taḥmīd, tahlīl, tasbīḥ through the day

t: Yawm ʿArafa
p: Duʿāʾ al-Maʾthūr of Grandshaykh — highly recommended for forgiveness and the gaze upon the reader

t: Hijrī New Year
p: End-of-year and new-year duʿāʾ

t: Birth of Shāh Naqshband
p: Recite the Ḥizb Qudsiyya as a gift to his memory

t: Ṣafar practice
p: Daily for protection and preservation: Shahāda ×3 · Astaghfiru-llāh ×300 · Sūrat al-Fīl ×7 · Āyat al-Kursī ×7 · Ṣadaqa every day with the intention of removing troubles · Ḥizb al-Wiqāya

t: Last Wednesday of Ṣafar — adab of Grandshaykh
p: After sunrise: 2 rakʿas Ṣalāt al-Ḥifẓ, Ikhlāṣ ×3 after Fātiḥa in each; Shaykh Adnan adds istighfār ×15 before Fātiḥa then ×10 at each posture · Shahādatayn ×3 · Istighfār ×300 · Fātiḥa ×1 · Āyat al-Kursī ×7 — blow and wipe over the body · Sūrat al-Fīl ×7 with taʿawwudh and basmala each time, blowing over self, family and house · Ihdāʾ to the Prophet ﷺ and the masters (al-Fātiḥa) · Give ṣadaqa befo

t: Mawlid al-Nabī ﷺ
p: Recite the Mawlid of Grandshaykh ʿAbdallāh al-Fāʾiz (al-Daybaʿī / al-Barzanjī)

t: ʿUrs of Shaykh ʿAbd al-Qādir al-Jīlānī
p: Al-Fātiḥa; Ṣalāt al-Kubrā and Qādirī awrād

t: Passing of Mawlana Shaykh Nazim (7 May 2014)
p: Ṣalāt al-Khuṣūṣ for Mawlana; his personal duʿāʾ after Khatm al-Khwājagān

t: Remembrance of Mawlana Shaykh Adnan Kabbani
p: Fātiḥa or any free offering of Qurʾān and adhkār

t: ʿUrs of Grandshaykh ʿAbdallāh al-Fāʾiz al-Dāghistānī (30 Sep 1973)
p: Fātiḥa; his Duʿāʾ al-Maʾthūr and as-Sayyid ad-Duʿāʾ

t: Laylat al-Barāʾa — night of 15 Shaʿbān
p: Sūrat Yā Sīn ×3: first for rizq and not needing people; second for long life with strong īmān; third for protection from every affliction for us and the Umma · After each Yā Sīn the duʿāʾ of the night (posted on @MawlanaSultan) · The Grand Transmitted Duʿāʾ of Grandshaykh ʿAbdallāh · Khatm al-Khwājagān and dhikr · Tasābīḥ 4; Shukr 2 with Qunūt · 100 rakʿas in twos: first rakʿa Fātiḥa + Ikhlāṣ ×2,

ref: Occasion · month 8 day last Thursday night
t: Last Friday (Thursday night) of Shaʿbān
p: Mawlana Shaykh Nāẓim: many tajallīs descend this night — keep it with worship

t: Muḥarram wazīfa
p: Added to the daily dhikr: 40 Ṣalawāt Tunjīnā · 100 Ḥasbunā-llāhu Rabbunā-llāh · 100 Bismi-llāhi r-Raḥmāni r-Raḥīm · 100 Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ · 100–1000 ṣalawāt

t: Entering the Hijrī year
p: Fast the last day of Dhū al-Ḥijja and the first of Muḥarram (Ibn ʿAbbās: a year's fasting completed) · At the new moon: ghusl and 2 rakʿas sunnat al-ghusl to welcome the year · Duʿāʾ of farewell to the old year ×3 (Allāhumma mā ʿamiltu fī hādhihi s-sana…), then the duʿāʾ of the new year · End-of-year and beginning-of-year duʿāʾs

t: ʿĀshūrāʾ — 10 Muḥarram
p: Fast · Full ghusl (intending good health); kohl in the eyes; buy provisions for the home; charity to family and the poor · Ikhlāṣ ×1000; istighfār and lā ilāha illā-llāh 100 each; ṣalawāt ×1000 · Tasābīḥ 4; Shukr 2 · After Adab al-Ṭarīqa: 4 rakʿas Sunnat ʿĀshūrāʾ (between Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr) — each Fātiḥa + Ikhlāṣ ×11 · Ḥasbunā-llāhu wa niʿma l-wakīl ×70 · Duʿāʾ of ʿĀshūrāʾ ×7: Subḥāna-llāhi milʾa l-mī

t: Duties of Rabīʿ al-Awwal
p: Astaghfiru-llāh 70–700 · Ikhlāṣ 100–1000 · Lā ilāha illā-llāh 100–1000 · Ṣalawāt 100–1000 · Yā Munqidh al-Halkā ×40 · Lā ilāha illā anta subḥānaka innī kuntu mina ẓ-ẓālimīn ×100 · Dalāʾil — the day's ḥizb · Read the Mawlid in congregation

t: 12 Rabīʿ al-Awwal — wazīfa as a gift for the Mawlid
p: Ṣalawāt before and after · Recite ×11: Yā Allāh, Yā Raḥmān, Yā Ghafūr, Yā Raḥīm, Yā Ḥannān, Yā Mannān, Yā Dayyān, Yā Subḥān (Shaykh Muḥammad Ghawth Gwaliyari: a blissful state the whole year)

t: Duties of Dhū al-Ḥijja
p: Astaghfiru-llāh ×100 · Ikhlāṣ ×100 · Lā ilāha illā-llāh 100–1000 · Ṣalawāt 100–1000 · Yā Laṭīf ×100 · Yā Jabbār ×100 · Yā Ghaffār ×100 · Yā Muʿīn al-ʿĀjizīn ×100
